* Monitoraggio dei processi di preparazione, conservazione e distribuzione dei pasti;

jobs.description:
**Aufgaben**
------------

Join our interdisciplinary team and help the development, as well as benchmarking of DNA sample preparation workflows for genome mapping.

* During your internship, you will gain practical experience with fluorescence microscopy and the preparation, as well as characterization of microfluidic chips.
* You will process DNA samples, evaluate purification methods and support library preparation for next-generation sequencing.
* Furthermore, you will analyze and annotate microscopy data using suitable image processing, as well as data analysis tools. You will then discuss your findings with the team.
* In addition, you will plan and conduct your own experiments independently, evaluating the yield, as well as purity of the DNA and its reproducibility.
* Last but not least, you will explore how physical parameters influence DNA dynamics, with the possibility of developing this into a thesis topic.

----------------

Full stack quantum networks promise breakthroughs in secure communication, advanced measurements, and computing. A key challenge in their implementation is interconnecting long-lived quantum memories with fast computational nodes due to their difference in wavelengths, pulse durations, and encoding schemes. Our junior research group aims to develop photonic quantum interconnects that adapt these properties to establish seamless connectivity between diverse quantum systems over networks and long distances. By tailoring photon wave packets with highspeed electronics and (nonlinear) optics, we aim to enable efficient and coherent manipulation of quantum states. **Quantitative Imaging and Translational Modelling for PSMA Radioligand Therapy**
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*(ref. BAP-2026-674)*
  
*Laatst aangepast: 23/11/26*

You will join the Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging Research Group at KU Leuven and University Hospitals Leuven (UZ Leuven). The group is located within the Medical Imaging Research Center (MIRC), bringing together clinicians, engineers, physicists and data scientists.

##### **Project**

This PhD project is embedded in a research project supported by VLAIO (Flanders Innovation & Entrepreneurship), in collaboration with Johnson & Johnson, SCK CEN and other project partners. The project, TTRAM (Tumor Therapeutics Translational Models), aims to improve predictions of human efficacy, toxicity and dosing for solid-tumour therapies. It combines experimental models, preclinical and clinical imaging and biodistribution data, and mechanistic computational models. Your research will focus on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) radioligand therapy. As a PhD researcher, you will connect quantitative imaging and pharmacokinetic data with physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models and dosimetry. The aim is to better predict how PSMA-targeting radioligands distribute in the body and the resulting radiation doses received by tumours and organs, particularly the kidneys and salivary glands.

Your responsibilities will include

* Contributing to imaging studies in large animals using PET/CT, SPECT/CT and MRI, and integrating imaging findings with pharmacokinetic and tissue data.
* Curating and analysing retrospective imaging, biodistribution and dosimetry data from patients receiving PSMA radioligand therapy.
* Processing and segmenting medical images to quantify radioligand uptake and kinetics in tumours and organs.
* Developing and evaluating PBPK models for large-animal and human applications using experimental and clinical data.
* Linking PBPK predictions with organ and sub-organ dosimetry in collaboration with SCK CEN.
* Performing statistical analyses, assessing model performance and variability, and contributing to scientific publications and conference presentations.

##### **Profile**

We are looking for a motivated candidate with a strong quantitative and computational background and an interest in molecular imaging, pharmacokinetics and translational cancer research.

Required qualifications

* A master’s degree in biomedical engineering, bioinformatics, physics, medical physics, applied mathematics, computational science or a closely related quantitative discipline.
* A solid foundation in numerical methods and mathematical modelling.
* Programming experience in Python, MATLAB or a comparable language for scientific computing.
* Ability to work independently and collaborate in a multidisciplinary team.
* Proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

Assets but not required

* Experience with PET/CT, SPECT/CT, MRI, image processing or organ segmentation.
* Experience with model parameter estimation, sensitivity analysis or uncertainty analysis.
* Familiarity with PBPK or compartmental modelling, pharmacokinetics, dosimetry or numerical simulation.
* Experience with preclinical or clinical research, or statistical data analysis.

##### **Offer**

We offer

* A PhD position at KU Leuven within TTRAM, with close collaboration with UZ Leuven, SCK CEN, Johnson & Johnson and the other project partners.
* Training in quantitative molecular imaging, translational PBPK modelling and dosimetry, with access to imaging and research infrastructure.
* The opportunity to contribute to patient-specific modelling for radioligand therapy in a multidisciplinary research environment.
* Opportunities for scientific publications and presentations at international conferences.
* A competitive salary and benefits package in accordance with KU Leuven regulations.

You will join the Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging Research Group at KU Leuven and University Hospitals Leuven (UZ Leuven). The group is located within the Medical Imaging Research Center (MIRC), bringing together clinicians, engineers, physicists and data scientists.

##### **Project**

This PhD project is embedded in a research project supported by VLAIO (Flanders Innovation & Entrepreneurship), in collaboration with Johnson & Johnson, SCK CEN and other project partners. The project, TTRAM (Tumor Therapeutics Translational Models), aims to improve predictions of human efficacy, toxicity and dosing for solid-tumour therapies. It combines experimental models, preclinical and clinical imaging and biodistribution data, and mechanistic computational models. Your research will focus on prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) radioligand therapy. As a PhD researcher, you will connect quantitative imaging and pharmacokinetic data with physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models and dosimetry. The aim is to better predict how PSMA-targeting radioligands distribute in the body and the resulting radiation doses received by tumours and organs, particularly the kidneys and salivary glands.

* Contributing to imaging studies in large animals using PET/CT, SPECT/CT and MRI, and integrating imaging findings with pharmacokinetic and tissue data.
* Curating and analysing retrospective imaging, biodistribution and dosimetry data from patients receiving PSMA radioligand therapy.
* Processing and segmenting medical images to quantify radioligand uptake and kinetics in tumours and organs.
* Developing and evaluating PBPK models for large-animal and human applications using experimental and clinical data.
* Linking PBPK predictions with organ and sub-organ dosimetry in collaboration with SCK CEN.
* Performing statistical analyses, assessing model performance and variability, and contributing to scientific publications and conference presentations.

We are looking for a motivated candidate with a strong quantitative and computational background and an interest in molecular imaging, pharmacokinetics and translational cancer research.
